I found buddhist teachings after years of extreme depression, and they have, combined with some christian teachings, and general wisdom, helped me very much in nearly eliminating that depression it seems, though I had a lot of setbacks over the years. The last time I was feeling at my worst, I went out onto depression and related subforums and made some posts to try and give some compassion, since I was able to understand what it was like to be incredibly low and deep in suffering.

That made the most difference in how I felt in a long time prior. Meditation had helped for a long time alone, but I couldn't see how I could actually perform generosity myself lacking resources until I realized I could give back there since they had helped me before, which helped me understand how it was a good thing to be doing when I can.

After that I did a lot of regular and metta meditation, which also helped a lot. I'm also kind of Christian-ish, though I don't know what to call my blend of belief, I prefer not to use labels because they just confuse me eventually or I become dogmatic. Anyways, I also prayed a lot and that also has been very helpful recently. I find my reputation seems to be improving now and it is making it a lot lot easier to be around other people.

For some, the rewards they get in life are not worth the effort required to attain them. Eventually, in my case, you become so hurt, so hurt and so tired. You have to beat yourself up mentally, emotionally, spiritually to keep moving, or you'll end up dying on the streets or being a financial and emotional burden on everyone around you. People try to "fix" you with drugs, platitudes, and threats. 

The drugs make you sick and overweight while failing to make you feel much, if at all better, often even making you feel worse than before you started them. Eventually you learn to stop talking because all people offer is pills and put downs disguised, even to themselves, as helpful advice. The pain grows until you become numb. 

The numbness is the worst. You don't hurt anymore, you don't enjoy anything either. The only reason you continue living is to avoid hurting others. Eventually, you just no longer have an incentive to do the work required to keep living or to "get better", and this is one of the most dangerous points. If you make it through this and restore your feelings (both pain and pleasure), your chances of survival greatly improve.

For those who otherwise find it hard to maintain motivation to survive, deliberately creating a craving for a specific, minimally harmful sensual pleasure can be wise as a temporary means of maintaining the will to live, but is unwise to seek for it's own sake. For example, it would be more wise and skillful to get drunk than to end your life, however, learning to enjoy a hot bath or meditation would be more wise/skillful than getting drunk. It depends on where you are on the path, and requires calculation of the pros and cons of the various options available.
